sections.text: Every device online supposedly needs a unique IP address. Yet, the world’s largest websites intentionally give hundreds of servers around the globe the exact same address using a system called Anycast.
When you load a webpage, the internet’s routers don't search the globe. They simply hand your request to the nearest physical clone, using the shortest road on the map.

This clever duplication absorbs massive traffic spikes, neutralizes cyberattacks by scattering the load, and ensures that if a Paris server fails, London instantly absorbs your traffic without a hiccup.
The internet gets faster by making its destinations identical.
